compliance.seismic: Complies with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per GR-63, Issue 4 (Table 22)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation up to 3048 m (10,000 ft) (Table 22)

features.macsec: IEEE 802.1AE MACsec on all Gigabit and 10 Gigabit Ethernet ports, 88 Gbps of encryption
features.optics-qsfp: the rear uplink ports take QSFP+ transceivers. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
features.optics-sfp-plus: the front uplink ports take SFP and SFP+ transceivers, singly or mixed. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
features.uplink-ports: four SFP or SFP+ ports on the front and two QSFP+ ports on the rear
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 switches. The QSFP+ ports are Virtual Chassis ports by default

management.console: RJ-45 console on the rear panel and Mini-USB Type-B console on the front, both labelled CON
management.oob: management Ethernet RJ-45 on the rear panel, with a Link/Activity lamp and a Status lamp
management.usb: one USB port on the rear panel

physical.depth-with-power-supply: 382.4 mm (15.05 in.) with a power supply installed (Table 3)
physical.weight: 4.76 kg (10.49 lb) without power supplies or fan modules (Table 3)
physical.width-with-brackets: 482 mm (19 in.) with the mounting brackets attached (Table 3)

power.poe-budget-w: 1440 W with two 920 W supplies, 740 W with one (Table 1)
power.poe-standard: PoE+ on all 48 ports, at most 30 W per port (Table 11)
power.power-current-max: 12 A at 100 VAC and 6.5 A at 240 VAC (Table 19)

ac.description: The switch as shipped: one 920 W AC supply in slot 0, a blank panel over slot 1 and two fan modules. Airflow is front to back.

description: Juniper EX3400-48P, a 1U access switch with 48 10/100/1000BASE-T ports that all supply PoE+. It has four SFP or SFP+ uplink ports and a Mini-USB console port on the front. The rear has two QSFP+ uplink ports, a management port, an RJ-45 console port, a USB port, two fan modules and two power supply slots. It ships with one 920 W AC supply, and a blank panel covers the second slot.

gaps.wanted: The front Mini-USB Type-B console, labelled CON, is drawn as decor and not placed as a port. The DCIM exporter has no route for a Mini-USB console part, and the guard test that holds every port part to the exporter fails until it has one. A change to dcim_export.py that exports a Mini-B console as a usb-mini-b console port would let the port be placed.

A per-port vocabulary for the Status lamp. Table 8 gives it four meanings that depend on the mode the Factory Reset/Mode button chose, so the jack keeps the component's default off, link and activity states, and the mode lamps carry the meaning.

The size of the CLEI code label and the Serial Number ID Label on the rear plate between fan 1 and power supply 0 (Figure 3 callouts 8 and 9). The plate and its corner marks are drawn as one grey rectangle.
The depth of a power supply and of a fan module. Table 3 gives a chassis depth of 350.0 mm with no supply and 382.4 mm with one, and the guide gives no dimension for the modules.
The Junos interface names (ge-0/0/n, xe-0/2/n and the QSFP+ names). This guide names only the PIC numbers in Table 2, 0 for the RJ-45 ports, 1 for the QSFP+ ports and 2 for the SFP+ ports.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

esd.description: the rear wrist-strap ESD point (Figure 3 callout 6)

attrs.redundancy-note: Both fan modules must be installed and working for normal cooling (fan removal topic)

grounding.description: the rear earthing terminal, two 10-32 screws for a two-hole lug (Table 41)

mgmt.mixed: the management corner - the out-of-band RJ-45, the RJ-45 console, the USB port and the Factory Reset/Mode button

mode-leds.description: SPD, DX, EN and PoE port mode lamps (Table 8). The Factory Reset/Mode button chooses which one shows

attrs.redundancy-note: 1+1 - the switch ships with one supply and takes a second. In the EU, Egypt, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Korea and South Africa the guide requires the redundant supply (Table 11 note)

qsfp-leds.description: A Link/Activity lamp and a Status lamp under each rear QSFP+ port. Table 7 - the Link/Activity lamp blinks green with traffic and is steady green with a link and no traffic. Table 9 - the Status lamp is steady when the 40-Gigabit port is up and unlit when it is down

qsfp-plus.description: Two rear QSFP+ uplink ports labelled 0 and 1. They are Virtual Chassis ports by default

rj45.description: 48 PoE+ ports labelled 0 to 47, the even ports on the upper row

sfp-plus.description: Four front uplink ports labelled 0 to 3. Each takes an SFP or an SFP+ transceiver

status-leds.description: SYS, ALM and MST chassis lamps (Table 4)

uplink-leds.description: A Link/Activity lamp and a Status lamp beside each front uplink port. Table 7 - the Link/Activity lamp blinks green with traffic and is steady green with a link and no traffic. Table 9 - the Status lamp is steady at 10 Gbps, blinking at 1000 Mbps, and unlit when the port is down

name: ex3400-48p

chassis.note: Table 3 - height 1.72 in. (4.37 cm), width 17.4 in. (44.1 cm), or 19 in. (48.2 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 13.78 in. (35 cm) with no power supply installed and 15.05 in. (38.24 cm) with one. The body of 441.0 mm is the metal between the bracket fold lines, and the 43.7 mm height is the metric figure as printed. The depth carried is the 350.0 mm of the bare chassis, and the supply adds the rest. Weight is 10.49 lb (4.76 kg) without supplies or fan modules.

color.note: photo-measured - median of the bare face between the port block and the bottom edge in the front photograph, #9ea1a5, darkened to #8c9094 for the face as a whole; the uplink plate is darker (#6b6f73). The rear and the fan and supply colours are sampled the same way.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's Figure 2 draws the printing too small to read, so the photograph wins for every legend. On the EX3400-48P the photograph prints "EX3400 PoE+" beside the Junos badge. The EX3400-48T photograph prints "EX3400" and still prints the POE lamp legend, while Table 8 says the PoE lamp is not available on a model without PoE; the legend and lamp are drawn on every model and the POE lamp is simply never lit on the T models.

ears.note: Mounting topics - two brackets and eight screws ship in the box and mount along the front or the rear of the side panels. The separately orderable four-post rack-mount kit holds flush and 2-in.-recess front-mounting brackets, side rails and rear blades. The recess is 2 in. (50.8 mm). The guide gives no part number for the four-post kit or for the wall-mount kit, so neither is listed under kits, and the guide's figures place the brackets without a measurable fold line, so only the recess has an `at`.

earthing.note: Table 41 - the EX3400 earthing terminal is on the rear panel, with two 10-32 screws and a two-hole lug. Figure 3 callout 4. The hole spacing is not stated in the guide; the photograph puts the two holes 16.0 mm apart. They are juniper/ex3400-ground-pair@1, two 10-32 screws on the 5/8 in. (15.875 mm) pitch of a two-hole lug, on the lighter plate that the photograph shows.

fru-bays.note: Table 2 and the guide's field-replaceable units topic - power supplies and fan modules are hot-removable and hot-insertable FRUs seated in bays, as are transceivers. The switch ships with one power supply and two fan modules (Table 36). With one supply the switch must be powered off before the supply is removed. Both fan modules must be installed for normal cooling. A supply and the fans must have the same airflow direction.

port-lamps.note: Figure 7 - each RJ-45 jack has two lamps, a Link/Activity lamp at the left corner and a Status lamp at the right corner of its keyway side. The common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Figure 8 - each SFP+ uplink has a Link/Activity lamp left of its number and a Status lamp right of it. The photograph shows them as tall light-pipe slots, drawn as common/led-rect@1 turned 90. The Status lamp on a jack shows speed, duplex, enabled or PoE state according to the mode lamps, so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: The legends under each column pair read 0 and 1, then 2 and 3, up to 46 and 47, so the upper jack of a column is the even port and the lower the odd one. The guide labels the ports 0 through 47. The uplink cages are printed 0 to 3 under the cages on the front, and the rear QSFP+ ports 0 and 1. Interface names such as ge-0/0/0 are not printed on the metal and are not stated in this guide, so none is recorded.

ports.note: Table 1 and Figure 2 give 48 RJ-45 ports in four blocks of 6 columns by 2 rows, and four uplink cages. The photograph gives their place. The 24 jack openings of the top row start at 47, 94, 141, 188, 235 and 282 px for the first block and at 345, 640 and 935 px for the next three. The in-block step of 14.1 mm is read against the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch, and the registry value is used. The block step of 88.8 mm is fitted so that the last jack ends at 1207 px as measured. The two rows stand 14.0 mm apart, fitted so that each row's jack opening overlays the photograph, with the upper row turned 180 so that its keyway and lamp tabs face up, as photographed. The four SFP cages start at 1226 px (363.7 mm) and abut on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch, 4 cages in 58.3 mm against 57.0.

power.note: Table 11 - the EX3400-48P consumes at most 120 W, and offers 1440 W for PoE with two 920 W supplies or 740 W with one. Table 19 gives 12 A at 100 VAC and 6.5 A at 240 VAC. The 120 W is the switch's own maximum, and the PoE budget is a separate figure and is not added to it.

rear.note: Figure 3 and the rear photograph, read at 3.327 px/mm across and 3.30 px/mm down. From the left, the management corner holds the MGMT RJ-45 over a USB-A port, then the CON RJ-45, a lighter plate with two earthing holes, the earth symbol, two QSFP+ cages marked 0 and 1 with a lamp slot pair under each, and the ESD socket. Then come fan 0 at 133.7 mm and fan 1 at 182.0 mm, a label plate for the CLEI code and serial number labels, power supply slot 0 at 271.7 mm and slot 1 at 354.4 mm.

rear-modules.note: Both power supply bays are drawn at the supply's own 71.2 by 39.0 mm face, measured on slot 0. The blank panel in slot 1 is photographed 76.6 by 41.0 mm because it overlaps the frame of the slot, and is drawn at the supply size so that it fills the same bay. Slot 1's position is the slot 0 position plus the 82.7 mm spacing of the two numerals.

scale.note: Gate 1 - the front photograph is a straight-on studio shot. The face measures about 1467 px across and 145 px high in the 1500 px wide file. Against 441.0 by 43.7 mm that is 3.327 px/mm across and 3.32 px/mm down, 0.2 percent apart, so the photograph is orthographic and carries geometry. The rear photograph agrees (3.327 across, 3.30 down). Positions below are read at that scale, so each is good to about 0.4 mm. Every figure read off a picture is estimated.

sources.note: EX3400 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2026-01-09 (317 pages): Tables 1 to 3, 10 to 13 and 19, Figures 1 to 4 and 7 to 10, the packing list (Table 36) and the mounting topics. Juniper image-library studio photographs ex3400-48p-front-high and ex3400-48p-rear-high, straight on, which supply every position below. The HPE PSNow datasheet (a50014095enw) did not answer from this host, so no datasheet figure is used. The community NetBox elevations for the EX3400-48P and -48T were used only to count and to compare the 150 W supply's face with the 920 W one; no dimension comes from them. The guide is copyright Juniper Networks, 2026, all rights reserved, and the studio photographs come from the maker's public image library; no terms of use are stated on the files. Nothing of either is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. End of life was searched on 2026-10-21: only reseller pages for Juniper support bundles (the B-EX3400-...-E part numbers, announced 2020 and 2023) came up and no Juniper notice for the hardware, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: Figure 5 and Table 4 give the chassis lamps SYS, ALM and MST. Figure 10 and Table 8 give the port mode lamps SPD, DX, EN and PoE and the Factory Reset/Mode button that switches them. The lamps are read off the photograph at the right end (x 426.1 and 432.2 mm, y 5.0 to 18.5 step 4.5). The mode button sits below the bracket line that joins the four mode lamps.
